subtopics.title: Forces Are Interactions — the Cast Around the Box

questions.question: The weight of the 8 kg box (using g = 9,8 m/s²) is:
options: 8 N downward
78,4 N downward
9,8 N downward
78,4 kg downward

questions.question: Mass and weight differ because:
options: Weight is the amount of matter; mass is a force
Both are vectors measured in newtons
Mass is the amount of matter (a scalar); weight is the gravitational force on it (a vector)
Mass shrinks on the Moon while weight stays the same

questions.question: Before a force may appear on the diagram, you must be able to:
options: Name the object responsible for the push or pull
Show that the box moves in that direction
Prove the force is larger than friction
Convert it to kilograms

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a real force on the sliding box?
options: The weight from the Earth
The normal force from the floor
Friction from the rough floor
A forward 'force of motion' keeping it going

questions.question: In a free-body diagram the object appears as:
options: A sketch of the box with the floor and strap included
An arrow showing where it is going
A single dot with every force arrow starting on it
A rectangle containing the force values

questions.question: The applied-force arrow for our box must be drawn:
options: At 25° above the horizontal, with the angle clearly marked
Straight up from the dot
At 25° below the horizontal
Horizontally forward

questions.question: Friction on the forward-sliding box is drawn:
options: In the direction of the pull
Horizontally backward, opposing the sliding
Straight down
At 25° backward and upward

questions.question: Which inclusion would COST credit on a free-body diagram?
options: A labelled friction arrow
The marked 25° angle
A velocity arrow drawn among the forces
An arrowhead on every force

subtopics.title: Reading the Physics Off the Diagram — Constant Velocity

questions.question: 'Constant velocity' tells you that:
options: The net force on the box is zero — all forces balance (Newton's first law)
The applied force must be the biggest arrow
Friction has vanished
The box accelerates gently

questions.question: The horizontal balance for the box reads:
options: N = w
F_applied sin 25° = f
F_applied = f
F_applied cos 25° = f

questions.question: Why is the normal force LESS than 78,4 N in this problem?
options: Movement always reduces the normal force
The strap's vertical component (F_applied sin 25°) helps lift the box, so the floor pushes less
Friction cancels part of the weight
It is not less — N always equals w

questions.question: Why does pulling at an upward slant make a box easier to drag (in later grades)?
options: The box's mass decreases while pulled
Slanted forces are always stronger
A smaller normal force means less friction, since friction depends on the normal force
Friction acts upward when the strap is angled

subtopics.title: The Method, the Error Museum, and the Road Ahead

questions.question: The systematic hunt for forces begins with:
options: The applied force
Gravity (always present), then every object touching the body
Friction
The largest force

questions.question: Friction always opposes:
options: The relative sliding between the surfaces
The applied force, whatever its direction
The normal force
The weight

questions.question: A free-body diagram must show:
options: Forces exerted BY the object on its surroundings
All objects in the problem on one diagram
Only horizontal forces
Forces acting ON the chosen object only — one object per diagram

subtopics.title: Who Is Actually Pulling on the Box?

questions.question: Hauling a trommel down a corridor, which four objects act on it?
options: The Earth, the air, the walls and the strap
The strap only
The Earth, the floor, the strap and the rough surface
The Earth and the person's energy

questions.question: Weight equals mass times gravitational acceleration. For the 8 kg box that is:
options: 78,4 N, straight down
8 N

questions.question: Which statement about mass and weight is correct?
options: Weight stays 78,4 N on the Moon; the mass shrinks
Both are measured in kilograms
Both would change equally on the Moon
Mass stays 8 kg on the Moon; the weight becomes smaller because the Moon pulls more gently

questions.question: Why is there no 'force of moving forward' on the sliding trommel?
options: Because friction has already cancelled it
Because no object supplies it — moving is something the trommel does, not something done to it
Because it only acts at high speed
Because it is too small to draw

questions.question: Turning a force diagram into a free-body diagram means throwing away:
options: The scenery — floor, strap and box outline — leaving a dot and the arrows
The force arrows
The arrowheads
The labels

questions.question: Recited in order, the four arrows leaving the dot are:
options: Up, down, up and down
Down for weight, up for the normal force, slanted up-and-forward for the strap, backwards for friction
Forward for motion, backward for friction
Only the strap and the weight

questions.question: An arrow without an arrowhead is a problem because:
options: It makes the diagram asymmetrical
Arrowheads are decorative but expected
It has not shown a direction, which is half of what a force is
It cannot be measured with a ruler

questions.question: Which item belongs on the free-body diagram?
options: The floor drawn under the dot
An arrow showing how fast the box slides
The strap drawn up to a shoulder
A labelled arrow for the normal force, starting at the dot

subtopics.title: Why the Slant Helps — and What "Constant Speed" Is Telling You

questions.question: 'Constant speed in a straight line' is the question telling you that:
options: Forward and backward effects are equal, and up and down effects are equal — nothing is winning
The strap supplies the biggest force
The trommel is about to stop
Friction no longer acts

questions.question: Pulling a garden cart by its raised handle does two jobs at once. Physics calls those jobs:
options: Tension and compression
Weight and normal force
The horizontal component and the vertical component of one force
Two separate applied forces

questions.question: The up-and-down balance for the box, in words, is:
options: The friction equals the weight
The floor's push plus the strap's upward part equals the weight
The floor's push always equals the weight
The weight plus the strap's upward part equals the floor's push

questions.question: Why is hauling a trommel with an up-slanted strap easier than pushing it flat?
options: The trommel loses mass when tilted
Straps remove friction completely
Pushing always doubles the friction
The upward pull lightens the floor's push, and less normal force means less friction
